prompt: My Compose screen draws under the status bar and the bottom nav gets covered by the gesture bar on a Pixel. How do I handle the insets properly?
note: Clear positive: edge-to-edge and window insets.

prompt: Set up the theme for our new Kotlin app so it picks up the user's wallpaper colors, with our brand green as the fallback on older phones.
note: Clear positive: dynamic color with a brand fallback.

prompt: The app looks broken on a Pixel Fold when it's unfolded. I want list and detail side by side on big screens and a single pane on phones.
note: Clear positive: adaptive layout, foldables.

prompt: Are the wavy loading indicator and the connected button group stable in material3 yet, or still behind an experimental opt-in? Which version do I need?
note: Clear positive: M3E API stability and versions.

prompt: Swiping back from my detail screen doesn't show the preview of the previous screen like other apps do. It's a Compose app with a custom nav setup.
note: Predictive back is a platform behavior. Motion is an acceptable extra.

prompt: Build a SwiftUI settings screen that shows a sidebar on iPad and collapses to a tab bar on iPhone.
note: Clear positive: navigation patterns.

prompt: The toolbar buttons in my Mac app should have that translucent glass look and blend into each other when they sit close together. What's the API for that?
note: Clear positive: Liquid Glass on a native app without naming it. The visual-styles stub is tolerable.

prompt: We're still building against iOS 26. What changes or breaks in our SwiftUI views when we move to the 27 SDK?
note: Clear positive: 26 to 27 migration.

prompt: Does this iPhone screen follow the HIG? It has a custom back button, 36pt tap targets and a fixed 15pt font everywhere.
note: Clear positive: HIG compliance, touch targets, Dynamic Type.

prompt: How do I make the checkmark icon bounce and fire a success haptic when a download finishes in my iOS app?
note: Symbol effects and haptics. Motion is an acceptable extra.

prompt: Railway keeps killing my Node worker in the middle of a job on every deploy. How do I let in-flight jobs finish first?
note: Clear positive: graceful shutdown and drain window.

prompt: I need a nightly job that sends digest emails from our Node backend on Railway. Should that be a cron service, or a queue with a worker?
note: Clear positive: cron vs worker vs queue.

prompt: Move our railway.toml to whatever the current config format is, and add a health check endpoint to the Express API while you're there.
note: Clear positive: deploy config migration, health checks.

prompt: Our Fastify API started throwing 'too many connections' against the Supabase database after we scaled to four replicas. Should we be going through the pooler?
note: Clear positive: Postgres connection modes.

prompt: In my Express API, how do I check that the bearer token the mobile app sends is a real signed-in Supabase user?
note: Clear positive: JWT verification on a standalone API server.

prompt: Do a full sweep of this repo before I merge to main and tell me what's wrong. Don't fix anything, just list it by severity.
note: Clear positive: pre-merge sweep, report only. Platform skills are fine as extras.

prompt: Check our auth and API layer for security holes: leaked keys, tables without RLS, anything logging user emails.
note: Clear positive: security category.

prompt: Is the Figma file ready to hand over to the developers? Go through it and flag whatever's missing.
note: Figma handoff check. code-audit has the checklist and report format, figma-design-system owns the gates. Either order, code-audit required.

prompt: Find dead code and any hardcoded hex colors or pixel values that should be tokens across the app. Report only.
note: Clear positive: dead code and hardcoded design values.

prompt: Go through the render callback in our C++ synth engine and flag anything that allocates or takes a lock.
note: Audio thread category in a non-Rust codebase.

prompt: I need a primary and an accent for a new brand. Thinking something like those old Swiss posters: strong red, lots of black and white.
note: Clear positive: choosing brand colors, Swiss style.

prompt: Pick me a yellow that works next to a deep blue for a poster-style landing page, and tell me whether black text on it passes AA.
note: Clear positive: pairing and contrast.

prompt: Give me a warm gray ramp for backgrounds, borders and text, with light and dark values, as CSS variables.
note: Clear positive: neutral ramps written as CSS tokens.

prompt: Put together a Bauhaus-inspired palette for a music app: the three primaries plus neutrals, mapped to surface, text and accent roles.
note: Clear positive: Bauhaus triad, semantic mapping.

prompt: We don't have brand colors yet. Suggest a restrained mid-century palette for the design system, and say which color should carry the primary action.
note: Clear positive: picking colors for a design system.

prompt: Start a new Figma file for our Android and web app. Variables first, then components, then screens.
note: Clear positive: starting a design system file.

prompt: Pick up where we left off in the design file. The components page is half done and the buttons are missing pressed and disabled states.
note: Clear positive: resuming a file, component states. 'Design file' without the word Figma.

prompt: Set up the variable collections with light and dark modes in Figma so Dev Mode shows the right CSS names.
note: Clear positive: collections, modes, code syntax.

prompt: Recreate our live iOS app in Figma, screen by screen, so we have a source file again.
note: Clear positive: replicating a live app.

prompt: Are we done with the mockups? Which screens does the file still need before I can call the design work complete?
note: Deciding whether design work is done. No tool named, so this leans on when_to_use.

prompt: Pin the hero section while the product image scales up and the copy fades in as you scroll, then release it. We're using GSAP.
note: Clear positive: ScrollTrigger choreography.

prompt: Should the drag-to-dismiss on our bottom sheet use a spring or an ease-out, and how long should the backdrop fade take?
note: Clear positive: spring vs ease, duration bounds. No platform named.

prompt: I want a particle field behind the landing page that reacts to the mouse. Three.js, on WebGPU where it's available.
note: Clear positive: Three.js particles.

prompt: When you click a card in our Next.js app it should grow into the detail page instead of hard cutting to it.
note: Clear positive: shared-element page transition, View Transitions.

prompt: What do we do with all our animations when someone has reduce motion turned on? I want one policy for iOS, Android and web.
note: Clear positive: reduced-motion policy across platforms.

prompt: I get 'future cannot be sent between threads safely' when I spawn this tokio task. It holds a MutexGuard across an await.
note: Clear positive: async and Send bounds.

prompt: Set up a new cargo workspace with three crates and CI that fails on warnings and on vulnerable dependencies.
note: Clear positive: workspace setup and CI gates.

prompt: Which crate should I use for a lock-free queue between the cpal callback and the UI thread?
note: Clear positive: audio-thread crates.

prompt: Take a look at this axum handler module. I'm not happy with the error types and there are unwraps everywhere.
note: Clear positive: reviewing Rust, error handling.

prompt: I want to call this Rust library from Swift over a C ABI. What's the right way to handle the unsafe boundary?
note: Clear positive: unsafe and FFI.

prompt: Make the dashboard look chunky and loud: thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat saturated color blocks.
note: Clear positive: Neo-Brutalism described, not named.

prompt: Redo the features section as rounded tiles of different sizes, like the summary slide at the end of an Apple keynote, with one big featured tile.
note: Clear positive: Bento Grid described, not named.

prompt: Give the login screen a green phosphor terminal vibe with scanlines.
note: Clear positive: Retro Computing.

prompt: Which look suits a meditation app better: the soft puffy pastel 3D one, or the one where everything is extruded out of the background color?
note: Clear positive: choosing between styles (Claymorphism vs Neumorphism), neither named.

prompt: I want the article reader to feel like nothing's there. Tons of whitespace, almost no chrome, no badges, no counters.
note: Clear positive: Calm / Anti-Distraction.

prompt: Use frosted translucent cards over a colorful gradient for the Android onboarding screens.
note: Glassmorphism on Android. The style is the request, the platform skill is a fine extra.

prompt: The product page is slow, LCP is around 4s on mobile. It's an App Router page that fetches from Supabase on every request. How should I cache it?
note: Clear positive: caching and Core Web Vitals.

prompt: Build an accessible modal with the native dialog element and a popover menu. No JS library.
note: Clear positive: semantic HTML.

prompt: Can I ship anchor positioning and :has() today, or do I still need fallbacks for Firefox and Safari?
note: Clear positive: is it safe to ship.

prompt: Users keep getting logged out at random. We use Supabase auth with cookies in Next.js and I think the session isn't being refreshed.
note: Clear positive: @supabase/ssr auth flow.

prompt: Set up an Astro blog with content collections and one interactive island for the search box.
note: Clear positive: Astro.

prompt: Add a strict Content-Security-Policy to the site without breaking the inline scripts Next injects.
note: Clear positive: security headers and CSP.

prompt: Animate the FAB morphing into a full-screen compose sheet in Jetpack Compose. Spring or tween?
note: Boundary. Owner: motion-design, which owns the spring-vs-ease decision and Compose AnimationSpec. android-platform is fine alongside for MotionScheme.

prompt: matchedGeometryEffect glitches when my card expands to full screen in SwiftUI. The image jumps at the end.
note: Boundary. Owner: motion-design, which lists matchedGeometryEffect. apple-platform is fine alongside.

prompt: Fade each section in as it scrolls into view using only CSS, no JavaScript.
note: Boundary. Owner: motion-design (scroll-driven animations). web-platform points motion technique there.

prompt: In a Next.js route handler I need to read the signed-in user's rows from Supabase. Which key and which client do I use?
note: Boundary. Owner: web-platform. Inside the Next.js request cycle means publishable key and @supabase/ssr. backend-conventions should stay out.

prompt: My Railway worker has to update rows for any user in Supabase, regardless of RLS. Which key do I use and how do I create the client?
note: Boundary. Owner: backend-conventions. Outside Next.js means the secret-key admin client. web-platform should stay out.

prompt: What color should I use for secondary text and separators in my SwiftUI list so it looks right in dark mode?
note: Boundary. Owner: apple-platform. System semantic colors win on a native app, so color-system should stay out.

prompt: Which container and on-container colors go on a tonal button in Compose?
note: Boundary. Owner: android-platform. Material color roles, not the curated palette.

prompt: How does color-mix() in oklch work, and how do I derive a hover shade from a base color with it?
note: Boundary. Owner: web-platform. Color-space technique, not which colors to choose. color-system says so in its last lines.

prompt: Does the palette we already have in tokens.css pass contrast for body text on each of the surface colors?
note: Boundary, uncertain. A project's own palette overrides color-system, so WCAG on the web is web-platform. color-system's contrast method is a tolerable extra.

prompt: Look over my Rust parser module and tell me what you'd change. The lifetimes feel wrong.
note: Boundary. Owner: rust-conventions. A review of Rust code is its job. code-audit is the checklist and report format for an audit, and nobody asked for one.

prompt: Run an audit on this Rust crate before I publish it.
note: Two skills. code-audit has the report format and tool gates, and routes any Rust crate to the rust-conventions checklist.

prompt: My axum service on Railway needs a health endpoint and has to drain open connections on SIGTERM.
note: Two skills. backend-conventions has the Railway behavior, rust-conventions the axum and Tokio shutdown code. The backend description says to pair them.

prompt: Check my Railway API for places where the secret key could leak or a JWT isn't verified.
note: Boundary. Owner: code-audit (security check, findings reported). backend-conventions holds the rules it checks against.

prompt: I want the Liquid Glass look on the nav bar of our marketing site.
note: Boundary. Owner: visual-styles. Any glass on Web or Android is Glassmorphism, and the style catalog routes it. apple-platform owns the real material and is a tolerable extra.

prompt: Add Liquid Glass to my custom floating tab bar in SwiftUI.
note: Boundary. Owner: apple-platform. The visual-styles entry is a stub that points there, so loading it is harmless.

prompt: Build the iOS tab bar with the glass material in our Figma file.
note: Boundary. Owner: figma-design-system for Figma mechanics. apple-platform owns the look.

prompt: In the Figma file, what should the variable for the card background be called?
note: Boundary. A Figma file question, plainly figma-design-system.

prompt: What should I name the CSS custom property for the card background so it lines up with the Swift and Kotlin names?
note: Boundary. Owner: figma-design-system, the single definition of token naming, even with no Figma file in sight.

prompt: Make the settings screen in our SwiftUI app neo-brutalist.
note: Boundary. Owner: visual-styles for a named style. apple-platform is fine alongside because platform behavior still applies.

prompt: Hero section with a giant headline whose words slide in one at a time as you scroll.
note: Two skills. Kinetic Typography is a style, and the stagger reveal is motion-design's SplitText and ScrollTrigger territory.

prompt: Start a Figma design system for our Android app in a claymorphism style.
note: Two skills. Figma process plus a named style.

prompt: Create the color variables in Figma from a Swiss poster palette: red primary, warm neutrals, light and dark.
note: Two skills. Figma variables plus palette values.

prompt: Draw an animated wavy gradient background behind the Android home screen with a runtime shader.
note: Boundary. Owner: android-platform (AGSL, RenderEffect). motion-design covers web shaders, so it's only a tolerable extra.

prompt: Write a Python script that removes duplicate rows from a CSV based on the email column.
note: Negative: general programming.

prompt: What's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore?
note: Negative: general concept question.

note: Negative: different backend stack.

note: Negative: different mobile stack. Shouldn't pull in android-platform or apple-platform.

note: Negative: different web stack. Vue Router and Firebase, nothing web-platform covers.

note: Negative: Go. Shouldn't pull in rust-conventions or backend-conventions.
